'''James Michael''' "'''M. J.'''" '''Walker Jr.''' (born March 28, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[College Park Skyhawks]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]].

==High school career==
[[File:20170329 MCDAAG M. J. Walker watches loose ball.jpg|thumb|left|Walker at the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
Walker attended [[Jonesboro High School (Georgia)|Jonesboro High School]] in [[Jonesboro, Georgia]]. He initially played football but he decided to focus on basketball after the summer of 2016. As a sophomore in 2014–15, Walker averaged 17.3 points, 4.5 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 3.0 steals leading Jonesboro to a 32–1 record and the 2015 Georgia Class 4A state championship. As a junior in 2015–16, Walker averaged 22.3 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 3.6 assists leading Jonesboro to a 28–5 record, regional title, and 2015 state title. As a senior in 2016–17, Walker averaged 27.8 points, 6.5 rebounds, and 2.4 assists leading Jonesboro to a 23–6 record.{{citation needed|date=July 2024}}

===Recruiting===
Walker was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] who received offers from [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], and [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]]. Walker committed to playing college basketball for Florida State.<ref>{{cite web|title=ESPN Recruiting Profile of M. J. Walker|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/198587/mj-walker|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=15 January 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
As a sophomore, Walker averaged 7.5 points and 2.2 rebounds per game. Florida State compiled a 29–8 record and reached the Sweet Sixteen of the NCAA Tournament.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McGahee |first1=Wayne |title=What will Florida State men's basketball look like next season? |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2019/03/29/florida-state-fsu-mens-basketball-2019-2020-preview-mfiondu-kabengele-trent-forrest-leonard-hamilton/3309603002/ |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=March 29, 2019}}</ref> At the conclusion of his junior season, Walker was named [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] Honorable Mention.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/8/athlete-awards-2020-acc-mens-basketball-award-winners-announced.aspx|title=2020 ACC Men's Basketball Award Winners Announced|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=March 9, 2020|accessdate=March 9, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 12.2 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game, earning Second Team All-ACC honors. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing the additional season of eligibility granted by the NCAA due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Staley |first1=Antwan |title=Florida State guard M.J. Walker officially declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/nolesports/2021/05/13/florida-state-guard-m-j-walker-officially-declares-2021-nba-draft/5080950001/ |access-date=November 1, 2021 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=May 13, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Westchester Knicks (2021)===
After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Walker signed with the [[New York Knicks]] on August 20, 2021,<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign M.J. Walker|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-mj-walker|website=NBA.com|date=August 20, 2021|access-date=August 21, 2021}}</ref> but was waived on October 16.<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks Waive Brandon Knight, Aamir Simms and M.J. Walker|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-waive-brandon-knight-aamir-simms-and-mj-walker|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 21, 2021}}</ref>  In October 2021, he joined the [[Westchester Knicks]] as an affiliate player.<ref>{{cite web |title=Westchester Knicks Announce Training Camp Roster |url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 1, 2021 |date=October 25, 2021}}</ref> Walker averaged 10.2 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game.

===Phoenix Suns (2021–2022)===
He signed a 10-day COVID-19 hardship exemption contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]] on December 30, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Zimmerman |first1=Kevin |title=Phoenix Suns sign M.J. Walker on 10-day hardship deal |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2950947/phoenix-suns-to-sign-m-j-walker-on-10-day-hardship-deal/ |access-date=December 30, 2021 |work=Arizona Sports |date=December 30, 2021}}</ref> He appeared briefly in two games for the Suns that season.

===Return to Westchester (2022–2023)===
On January 9, 2022, Walker was reacquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]]. On September 22, Walker resigned with the Knicks on a training camp deal but was waived a day later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 9, 2022|access-date=January 9, 2022}}</ref>

On October 24, 2022, Walker was named to the training camp roster for the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/westchester-knicks-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster/n-5892760|website=oursportscentral.com|title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2022-23 Training Camp Roster|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}}</ref>

===Vancouver Bandits (2023)===
On June 6, 2023, Walker signed with the [[Vancouver Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bandits Sign NBA-Experienced Guard MJ Walker|url=https://www.thebandits.ca/bandits-signed-nba-experiences-guard-mj-walker|website=TheBandits.ca|date=June 6, 2023|access-date=June 7, 2023}}</ref> However, he was released on July 8 after averaging 11.2 points through 9 games for the club.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vancouver Bandits Release MJ Walker|url=https://www.thebandits.ca/vancouver-bandits-release-mj-walker|website=TheBandits.ca|date=July 8, 2023|access-date=July 8, 2023}}</ref>

===Brampton Honey Badgers (2023)===
On July 29, 2023, Walker signed with the [[Brampton Honey Badgers]] ahead of the postseason.<ref>{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Warrener|title=NBA EXPERIENCED GUARD M.J. WALKER SIGNS WITH HONEY BADGERS AHEAD OF POSTSEASON PLAY|url=https://www.honeybadgers.ca/nba-experienced-guard-m-j-walker-signs-with-honey-badgers-ahead-of-postseason-play|website=HoneyBadgers.ca|date=July 29, 2023|access-date=July 30, 2023}}</ref>

===Saint-Quentin (2023–2024)===
On August 3, 2023, Walker signed with [[Saint-Quentin Basket-Ball|Saint-Quentin]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Saint-Quentin officialise l'arrivée de M.J. Walker|url=https://www.bebasket.fr/saint-quentin-officialise-larrivee-de-m-j-walker/|website=BEBasket.fr|date=August 3, 2023|access-date=August 6, 2023|language=French}}</ref>

===Greensboro Swarm (2024)===
On January 19, 2024, Walker joined the [[Greensboro Swarm]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Swarm Complete Transaction with Westchester Knicks|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/swarm-complete-transaction-with-westchester-knicks|website=NBA.com|date=January 19, 2024|access-date=January 20, 2024}}</ref>

===Canterbury Rams (2024)===
On March 12, 2024, Walker signed with the [[Canterbury Rams]] of the New Zealand [[National Basketball League (New Zealand)|National Basketball League]] (NZNBL) for the [[2024 New Zealand NBL season|2024 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Former NBA Guard MJ Walker Signs With Rams|url=https://canterburyrams.basketball/former-nba-guard-mj-walker-signs-with-rams/|website=canterburyrams.basketball|date=March 12, 2024|access-date=March 15, 2024}}</ref>

===Return to Greensboro (2024–2025)===
On October 27, 2024, Walker rejoined the [[Greensboro Swarm]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Greensboro Swarm Announce Training Camp Roster for 2024-25 Season|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-swarm-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2024-25-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on November 13, after one game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Greensboro Swarm Complete Multiple Transactions|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-swarm-complete-multiple-transactions|website=NBA.com|date=November 13, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}}</ref> However, he was re-signed six days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Greensboro Swarm Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Greensboro-Swarm/45/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 20, 2024}}</ref>

===College Park Skyhawks (2025–)===
On October 13, 2025, Walker signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hawks.com/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-guards-lamont-butler-deivon-smith-m-j-walker|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Guards Lamont Butler, Deivon Smith, & M.J. Walker|website=[[NBA]]|date=October 13, 2025|access-date=December 29, 2025}}</ref> However, he was waived the next day and would join the [[College Park Skyhawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/mj-walker-let-go-by-atlanta/|title=MJ Walker: Let go by Atlanta|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=October 14, 2025|access-date=December 29, 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
Walker played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States national under-18 team]] at the [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]] in [[Valdivia]], Chile. In four games, he averaged 2 points and 1.8 rebounds per game, helping his team win the gold medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/225983/James-Michael-Walker|title=James Michael Walker|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=March 20, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Walker is the son of James and Jackie Walker, and has an older sister, Amoni, who plays for [[Miles College]]. His father, James, played [[college]] basketball at Norfolk State University and his mother, Jackie, played women's [[college basketball]] for [[Hampton University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://seminoles.com/sports/basketball/roster/m-j-walker/|title=M. J. Walker at Florida State University|date=July 28, 2017 |publisher=Athletics at Florida State University|accessdate=15 January 2018}}</ref>
